# plar.txt format and operations

Version 1 is UTF-8 JSON, not a new programming language. The normative shape is [plar.schema.json](../../../runtime/pixl/plar.schema.json). A complete worked project is [the queue UI example](../../../resources/examples/plar-project/README.md). Read its source before its example requirements.

Top-level fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| version | `1` |
| project | `name` and concise `brief`; no absolute installation paths |
| coverage | Arrays `included`, `excluded`, `unresolved`; explicit scan boundary and blind spots |
| sources | Stable `id`, project-relative `path`, optional `sha256`; saves bind existing files without a hash |
| assets | Stable rows described below; an empty list is valid when the inspected scope requires no production art |

Each asset has `id`, `kind`, `purpose`, `status`, `consumers`, `existing`, `requirements`, `delivery`, `depends_on`, `questions`, `next`, and `evidence`. Optional `production` links `store`, `task`, `output`. Optional `references` names visual inputs as described below. Kind is a descriptive string; UI panels, fonts, atlases and normal maps need not pretend to be sprites here. Translate to the actual PIXL/provider contract during production.

- `consumers`: `{source, symbol, usage}`; source is an ID from the sources table. Symbol and usage explain the binding, not merely a filename.
- `references`: `{source, role, instructions}`; source is a bound source ID. Role is `style`, `identity`, `pose`, `layout`, `palette`, `mask` or `motion`. Instructions say what to preserve. These are optional for text-only briefs; a filename mentioned in a requirement is not provider image transport.
- `existing`: `{path, role}`; role explains reusable/placeholder/reference or other current use. Missing paths are reported, not rejected.
- `requirements`: `{property, value, authority, sources, reason}`. Value is JSON; authority is `requirement`, `observation`, `proposal`, or `unknown`. Sources is an array of source IDs. An empty array is useful for an explicit unsourced proposal/unknown; support adopted requirements with addressable evidence.
- `delivery`: `{path, checks}`; exact destination (file or package path) and applicable mechanical, visual and consumer/import checks.
- `depends_on`: other asset IDs; cycles and dangling IDs are rejected.
- `questions`: unresolved choices relevant to this asset. `next`: one actionable instruction.
- `evidence`: `{path, note}` links to retained results. Source-bind evidence that must remain byte-identical.
- `status`: `todo`, `in_progress`, `review`, `integrated`, or `deferred`. Status is authored by the host. File existence does not prove integration or quality.

All paths are relative to the consumer root and use forward slashes. Source hashes detect local drift; they do not prove the interpretation of the source. The reader reports changed/missing/unbound sources and missing files. It does not restamp changed sources, guess readiness, contact PixelLab or certify artistic quality. Refresh a hash only after re-reading and reconciling the dependent claims. Focused reads include the full transitive dependency rows and their issues, so a caller does not lose the style baseline or an unresolved source when delegating a dependent asset.

## MCP

`pixl_plar_read({})` returns the queue, project scope and source binding results. To select an asset:

```json
{"asset_id":"queue.working"}
```

Save through `pixl_plar_save` with `document` holding the complete JSON document and `expect` equal to the last returned file hash, or `"new"` for creation. Optional `path` defaults to `plar.txt`. A stale write is rejected; re-read and merge. Previous changed bytes are retained under `.pixl/plar-history/`. Keep independent queues in separate files when project scope requires it.

Use `pixl_commit({store,expect,document})` for a PX2 document with its next revision. The JSON record format uses `{"$ref":"id"}` and `{"$symbol":"value"}`. Exactly one of `document` or the existing `candidate` wire-file path is accepted. The same revision, dependency, evidence and acceptance checks apply. PLAR does not automatically invent PX2 decisions or criteria.

## CLI and portability

Resolve the plugin runner relative to this skill, then use its **absolute** path with the target project root:

```text
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar read --root /ABS/PROJECT
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar read --root /ABS/PROJECT --asset queue.working
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py plar save /ABS/document.json --root /ABS/PROJECT --expect new
python /ABS/PLUGIN/scripts/pixl.py commit /ABS/PROJECT/.pixl /ABS/plan.json --json --expect STATE_HASH --root /ABS/PROJECT
```

Copy/install the complete plugin, not the skill directory alone. Requirements and outputs stay in the consumer project. The CLI can support a host without MCP; the MCP server exposes the same deterministic operations when configured with that root.

## Focused delegation identity

A selected read returns `project_root`, `requirements_hash`, `asset`, full `dependencies`, relevant `sources`, `visual_references` and a derived `production` view. Source rows add `observed_sha256` and `absolute_path`; stored source paths remain portable and relative. The full queue's existing `hash` is still the compare-and-swap token for saves.

The requirements hash covers the selected asset and transitive dependency requirements, their bound/current source identities and project brief. It excludes status, next action, evidence lists, production-state links and absolute installation paths. It does not assert readiness or acceptance; read dependency status/issues separately. Changing a style reference changes this hash even before someone refreshes its saved source hash. An unrelated asset's queue progress does not.

This additive version-1 extension keeps existing documents valid. Use a runtime containing the reference-role extension to author documents with `references`; older closed-schema readers cannot interpret new fields.

## Selective refresh

Queue reads include `changes`: tracked source drift, direct and transitively affected asset IDs, and unaffected IDs. Pass `since` (CLI `--since`) with a retained prior PLAR byte hash to compare declarations as well. Saves return this comparison against the replaced version. Queue progress fields (`status`, `next`, `evidence`, `production`) are not requirement changes. Coverage changes are reported separately. History bytes are hash-checked before comparison. Use `since` on the whole queue, then select an affected asset; focused reads include `dependency_issues`.

This is conservative file/dependency impact, not a semantic code scanner. Re-read changed code and look for new states, consumers or dynamic paths. A shared source edit can affect several rows for review without requiring all their requirements or assets to change. Do not merely refresh hashes. Keep stable roles/IDs on destination moves; retain superseded work as deferred where applicable.

[First-candidate preparation](prepare.md) consumes a focused selection and the exact reviewed request/criteria artifacts, removing handwritten PX2 setup from that path.

## Allocation and production continuity

A focused read joins the selected row to its retained PX2 store. `production` reports
current task/output acceptance, selection identity, provider-bound pending jobs and
one next action. Missing or invalid state is an explicit diagnostic while the
requirements remain readable. Queue `status` remains an authored progress label.
`new_request_allowed` is only a local selection/pending-work advisory; preparation
still validates the exact reviewed request, current source identity and connection.

Single-output preparation links the resulting store/task/output and snapshot evidence
back to the row. A failed concurrent queue save leaves the prepared job intact; resume
the same preparation to repair its link. The default asset store is discoverable;
custom stores require the existing link or explicit store argument. Multiple outputs
need a deliberate choice of the delivery output.

Source changes require review of affected/dependent rows, not automatic replacement
of all art. For a revised contract, reconcile pending work on its original connection,
retain the reviewed new packet, then use `plar prepare --revise --expect STATE_HASH`.
The new generation is appended to the existing store; prior inputs, jobs, candidates
and verdicts remain. Use returned IDs. Historical acceptance describes its original
contract and cannot complete the newly selected generation.

\"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema\"\r\n}\r\n# PIXL/1 normative specification\r\n\r\nStatus: implemented version 1.0.0. PIXL is a project-specific, agent-operated UDL; this document is its decoder contract. The wire form has no human usability requirement. Host profiles are a separate translating layer. Reserved notation cannot silently acquire a new meaning.\r\n\r\n## Wire grammar\r\n\r\nInput is UTF-8, maximum 16 MiB. ASCII whitespace is insignificant outside literals. There are no comments, escapes, implicit coercions, expressions, interpolation, executable imports, or indentation semantics. Parsing is bounded to 64 nested value containers and 100,000 records. ASCII identifiers match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,95}`. IDs are case sensitive and document-unique.\r\n\r\n```ebnf\r\ndocument = \"PX1\", whitespace, revision, whitespace, { record, whitespace } ;\r\nrecord   = \"@\", identifier, \":\", kind, map ;\r\nmap      = \"{\", [ identifier, \"=\", value, { \";\", identifier, \"=\", value } ], \"}\" ;\r\nlist     = \"[\", [ value, { \",\", value } ], \"]\" ;\r\nvalue    = literal | reference | symbol | integer | list | map | \"+\" | \"-\" | \"?\" ;\r\nreference= \"@\", identifier ;\r\nsymbol   = identifier ;\r\ninteger  = [ \"-\" ], digit, { digit } ;\r\nliteral  = \"~\", unsigned-byte-count, \":\", exactly-that-many-UTF8-bytes ;\r\nkind     = one-uppercase-ASCII-letter ;\r\nrevision = unsigned-integer ;\r\n```\r\n\r\n`+` is true, `-` is false, `?` is absent/null. Integers are signed 64-bit; lengths and revisions are nonnegative. Floating-point wire values are intentionally absent: coordinates are integer pixels; duration is integer milliseconds; fractional quantities use declared fixed-point units in asset metadata, or opaque provider JSON at the boundary. A symbol and a literal with the same visible text are different values. A reference is never a string. Lengths count UTF-8 bytes, not characters. `~0:` is an empty literal. A literal may contain newlines, delimiters, backslashes or NUL without acquiring syntax. A malformed UTF-8 length boundary is an error. Duplicate fields are errors.\r\n\r\nCanonical encoding starts `PX1 <revision>\\n`, sorts records by ID and map fields by ASCII key, preserves list order, uses decimal integers without leading zeroes and one newline after each record. Canonical map/list values contain no insignificant whitespace. SHA-256 over canonical document bytes is the snapshot identity. SHA-256 over the canonical record bytes (without the trailing newline) is a record identity. Revision is not a record field. Noncanonical valid input can be normalized without changing its semantic values.\r\n\r\n## Semantic registry\r\n\r\nThe complete field/type dictionary is [`registry.json`](../pixl/registry.json). That machine-readable registry and this specification are normative together. Unknown kinds, fields and closed-enum values fail validation; extension requires a new explicit version. All fields are required unless marked optional in the registry. `tg` is an optional list of literal tags on every kind. Map payloads are permitted only in declared fields; they cannot override core fields.\r\n\r\nThe bundled operational knowledge library is `knowledge/library.px`. Its K `rq` prerequisites and `rk` failure conditions preserve the curated source conditions. `ap` atoms are generated from source applicability phrases with stable SHA-256 suffixes; their exact meanings are in the hash-bound `knowledge/applicability.json` source. They are domain symbols, not inferred new core language rules. Source JSON is retained for curation and host interchange; the compiled K/S/E graph is available directly to contextual operation.\r\n\r\n| Kind | Meaning | Operational replacement |\r\n|---|---|---|\r\n| A | actor and responsibility | ownership / agent role |\r\n| P | project and active visual contract | project design envelope |\r\n| S | source with digest and locator | reference tagging / provenance |\r\n| R | runtime/tool dependency with exact version locator | tech stack |\r\n| C | visual contract, dimensions, palette, view, sampling and alpha policy | art design document |\r\n| K | applicable knowledge method, procedure, checks, research and POC references | technical knowledge |\r\n| D | decision: `wh` who, `wt` what, `wr` where, `wy` why, `rs` research, `pc` proof | design rationale |\r\n| T | task, ownership, dependencies, decisions, inputs/outputs, state and evidence | work plan / TODO / dependency graph |\r\n| X | artifact/reference and its expected bytes, contract and metadata | asset manifest / content map |\r\n| E | evidence receipt, outcome, mode, file hash and bound record hashes | test/review result |\r\n| J | external job identity, request digest and observed state | tool execution memory |\r\n| N | resumption focus, next tasks and blockers at a specific revision | contextual handoff |\r\n\r\nReferences resolve within the document and must match the declared target kind. Task `dp` edges are directed from dependent to prerequisite and must be acyclic. Other reference cycles are legal (for example a decision and its proof) and closure uses visited IDs. Ready tasks are open tasks whose prerequisites are all done. Dropped prerequisites do not satisfy a dependency. Active/blocked/done tasks are not advertised as ready. A done task needs at least one current passing evidence receipt and all prerequisites done; those passing receipts must collectively bind every current `io` artifact record. A task cannot be done with no `io` artifact. Evidence binding `{rf=@id;dg=~64:<record-sha256>}` snapshots the full record, not its name. Any record change invalidates that binding. Passing evidence does not erase failing evidence.\r\n\r\nDecisions require nonempty research and proof lists, and nonempty who/what/where/why content. Their current proof receipts must collectively bind the decision record itself and its semantic dependency closure. Proof receipts may report failure: a decision can reject a failed method. A K with `pc` must have current receipts binding that method and its semantic sources; an active/done task requires passing receipts covering that scope. K methods without executed proof are retained as researched knowledge, but an agent must execute an applicable POC before adoption. A method's recipe is not an executed proof. Agents preserve conflicting observations in separate source/evidence records and resolve them through a new decision rather than overwriting history.\r\n\r\n**Semantic proof scope** traverses only `A/S/R/C/K/D/X`. It stops before workflow/project/proof kinds `P/E/T/J/N`, which would otherwise entangle mutable task states and proof history with the result being proved. X proof bindings must cover its scope, including the linked C. Link source/runtime/contract records directly when their content is part of the proof; a pointer through P does not bind that project's contents. K and D can point to E by ID while E binds their hash: the hash contains reference IDs, not recursive target hashes.\r\n\r\nEvidence `ob=+` marks a superseded receipt. Its original outcome, file and old bindings remain preserved; outdated record hashes are allowed only in superseded receipts. Such receipts never count for decisions, method adoption or completion. Store commits forbid modifying existing E fields except one-way supersession; add a new E ID for new execution. Receipt metadata is a caller assertion supported by retained files. Hash validation establishes identity and freshness, not cryptographic attestation that a model, service or test runner told the truth.\r\n\r\nFile checking is optional for structural validation and mandatory when accepting completion in a store. With a project root, X/E local paths and locally addressed S bytes must exist, remain within that root after symlink resolution, and match their declared SHA-256. URL sources are not downloaded by validation; their digest identifies a recorded snapshot and does not assert current remote truth. Source `ln` ranges are inclusive, one-based and valid for the local source. Empty palettes mean no exact palette restriction, not zero colors. C rules apply only to linked artifacts; source art can intentionally choose a different contract.\r\n\r\n### Explicit retention of imported library source revisions\r\n\r\nA project can opt into the versioned [library source retention operation](library-retention.md). It preserves the exact declared local S revision in project-owned storage before replacing an installed kit, or recovers it from a supplied original kit. If that S locator later changes or disappears, resolution may use its explicitly retained locator/digest entry. The retained bytes and original line range must pass the same checks; reports identify the old revision actually used. This does not relax X/E file checks or substitute old bytes for a different requested digest. No record, evidence binding or outcome is rewritten, and no old proof is promoted to evidence about a newer implementation.\r\n\r\n## Retrieval and drift\r\n\r\n`context(focus)` includes the focus, all project roots and their transitive references, and the focus's transitive reference closure. For T focus it also includes associated J records and handoffs mentioning the focus. This is a conservative correctness baseline; it never silently truncates a required dependency or decision. If canonical packet bytes exceed a requested byte budget it returns a budget error with the required size. Bytes are not claimed to equal model tokens. Large project roots should not reference every task: tasks point to their project. Returned subsets keep the original revision and validate as closed documents.\r\n\r\n`impact(id)` traverses reverse references transitively. The changed node itself is included. `ready` returns stable sorted task IDs. A content map is a query over X/S records and `tg`; a stack is a query over R; decisions over D. There are no duplicated authoritative Markdown TODO/stack state files. Source catalogs are derived indexes and can be rebuilt.\r\n\r\n## State publication\r\n\r\nA store contains `state.px`, immutable `history/<canonical-sha>.px`, and a temporary exclusive `.lock` while writing. Initialize once. A candidate must have exactly current revision + 1; caller must supply the current canonical hash. Under the lock, reload current state, compare revision/hash, validate the complete candidate and its files, write/fsync its history snapshot and a same-directory temporary state, then atomically replace state. The final state is the commit point. A crash may leave an unreferenced valid history snapshot or lock; it must not publish a partial document. A leftover lock fails with recovery guidance; it is never automatically broken while a writer might be alive. Filesystem snapshots provide local recovery, not distributed consensus or protection from a malicious filesystem writer. Direct manual state editing bypasses these guarantees and is unsupported for operation.\r\n\r\nTask transitions: open -> active/blocked/dropped; active -> blocked/done/dropped; blocked -> open/active/dropped; done -> open; dropped -> open. Unchanged states are allowed. Existing IDs cannot disappear or change kind during commit; close/drop records instead. Any change to a done task or its complete reference closure requires reopening that task. Supersede invalidated receipts with `ob=+`, retain their original bindings, add new receipt IDs after new execution, and redirect D/K/T evidence references deliberately. Revision increases are mandatory even for resumption changes.\r\n\r\nC describes raster dimensions and rendering intent. X of kind `code` or `report` associates with its production contract but is not interpreted as a raster image. X metadata is an opaque declared payload: the core validates wire values and references, not a target engine's atlas/rig schema. Domain knowledge recipes and appropriate project tools validate those additional contracts. A structural/file validation alone does not establish visual acceptance.\r\n\r\n## PixelLab boundary\r\n\r\nThe host retrieves the actual connected PixelLab tool input schema. PIXL prepares a validated intent with exact tool name, arguments, schema digest and request digest. JSON here is the MCP provider's interchange, not PIXL syntax. Preparation has no remote side effect. The host calls the provider and journals the observed real ID. Generation starts prepared -> submitted -> running -> succeeded/failed; submitted/running may become unknown when observation is lost. Unknown is not permission to recreate a paid job. Recovery requires observation of the existing job; there is no automatic generation retry. A generation result is an artifact candidate, not proof of quality or task completion.\r\n\r\nDurations/credits reported in research are estimates from a dated documentation snapshot. Discovered schemas take precedence over snapshots. PixelLab credentials remain in host secret configuration. This runtime does not impersonate PixelLab or invent job IDs. Its MCP server exposes local project tools only; the host connects the actual PixelLab MCP separately.\r\n\r\n## Verification boundaries\r\n\r\nThe suite verifies parsing, graph invariants, writes, request validation, job transitions, artifact measurements, deterministic method POCs and local MCP behavior. Image inspection hashes and measures one immutable in-memory byte snapshot, checks every frame's dimensions and cumulative pixel limit, and labels visual/engine acceptance unverified. Token measurements are encoding-specific comparisons with the same semantic payload, including bootstrap overhead separately. They are not a controlled LLM capability or artistic-quality study. A full live PixelLab job and target-engine visual acceptance must be recorded with real evidence before those outcomes are asserted.\r\n"}
